'''Kamitsukeno no Tamichi''' (田道, birth date unknown - 55th year of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku}}’s reign) was a warrior of the Nintoku court. His clan and title are not described in the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'', but the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'' refers to him as '''Tamichi no Kimi''' (田道公) with the kabane title of ''Kimi''.

== Overview ==

In the 53rd year of Emperor Nintoku's reign, {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla}} neglected its tribute obligations. Tamichi’s elder brother, {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬}}, was dispatched as an envoy to investigate. Later, Tamichi led a military force to defeat the Silla troops. During the campaign, he captured and brought back the inhabitants of four settlements.

In the 55th year of Nintoku's reign, Tamichi was sent to suppress a rebellion by the {{ill|Emishi|ar|إيميشي|ca|Emishi|cs|Emiši|de|Ezo (Volk)|es|Emishi|eu|Emishi|fa|امیشی|fr|Emishi|gl|Emishi|id|Emishi|it|Emishi|ja|蝦夷|ko|에조|nl|Emishi|no|Emishi|pl|Emishi|pt|Emishi|ru|Эмиси|sr|Емиши|tr|Emishi|uk|Емісі|wuu|虾夷|zh|蝦夷|zh_min_nan|Emisi|zh_yue|蝦夷|qid=Q932574|lt=Emishi}}, but he was defeated and killed at the Ishinomito waterway. After his death, his attendant gave Tamichi’s keepsake, a jade he had wrapped around his hand, to his wife, who, stricken with grief, took her own life. Later, when the Emishi desecrated Tamichi’s grave, a giant serpent emerged and attacked them, causing many fatalities.<ref>{{Cite book|lang=ja|author=Kudō Masaki|title=The Ancient History of the Emishi|publisher={{ill|Yoshikawa Kōbunkan|fa|یوشیکاوا کوبونکان|ja|吉川弘文館|ko|요시카와 홍문관|zh|吉川弘文馆|qid=Q4346755}}|year=2019|page=71}}</ref>

== Banknote Depiction ==
[[File:Early one yen banknote front and reverse.jpg|thumb|Front and reverse of an early one-yen banknote issued by the {{ill|Second National Bank of Japan|ja|第二国立銀行|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Second National Bank of Japan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11602278}}. The right of the front features Tamichi.]]
{{main|National Bank Notes of Japan#One Yen Note}}
In 1873 ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 6), Tamichi was depicted on the one-yen convertible banknotes issued by the National Bank.<ref name="uemura">Uemura Takashi, ''Portraits on Banknotes in Modern History,'' Yoshikawa Kōbunkan, 2015, pp. 66–67. ISBN 978-4-64-203845-4</ref>

Two theories exist regarding the design of the note: one suggests it depicts Kamitsukeno no Tamichi fending off a surprise attack by the Emishi, while the other posits it as depicting {{ill|Minamoto no Tametomo|en|Minamoto no Tametomo|qid=Q1339356|lt=Minamoto no Tametomo}} defending against Kudo Shigemitsu’s fleet. Notably, the figure is depicted with a disproportionately large head relative to the body, an unusual stylistic choice.<ref name="uemura"/>

== Legend ==
Legends about Tamichi are preserved at the {{ill|Saruka Shrine|arz|ساروكا جينجا|fr|Saruka-jinja|ja|猿賀神社|mr|सारुका जिंजा|qid=Q3473746|lt=Saruga Shrine}} in {{ill|Hirakawa, Aomori|en|Hirakawa, Aomori|qid=Q695930|lt=Hirakawa, Aomori}}, {{ill|Aomori Prefecture|en|Aomori Prefecture|qid=Q71699|lt=Aomori Prefecture}}, and the {{ill|Toriya Shrine|ja|鳥屋神社}} in {{ill|Ishinomaki|en|Ishinomaki|qid=Q270814|lt=Ishinomaki}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|en|Miyagi Prefecture|qid=Q47896|lt=Miyagi Prefecture}}.<ref>http://saruka.webcrow.jp/</ref><ref>https://www.miyagi-jinjacho.or.jp/jinja-search/detail.php?code=310010081</ref>

== Genealogy ==
According to the ''Nihon Shoki,'' Tamichi was the son of {{ill|Aratawake|ja|大荒田別命}} and the younger brother of {{ill|Takehase|ja|竹葉瀬}}.
